contract.idempotency: Every skill that mutates external state MUST create one globally unique operationId and record an intent before executing each effect. The intent includes operationId, effect name, remote identity, fixed-point/revision fence, approval token, and checkpoint. Retries MUST reconcile the remote state by those fields before executing; an unknown outcome is a first-class state and MUST NOT be silently re-executed. Existing matching state is adopted; duplicate PRs, comments, merges, closes, pushes, and updates are forbidden. Side effects before an interrupt or pause must be safe to resume from their last checkpoint.
contract.saga: Mutating workflows are sagas: plan -> preflight -> effect -> reconcile -> commit-checkpoint, with a checkpoint before and after every effect. Each effect has separate approval, bounded compensation, and rollback evidence. Compensation may undo only effects owned by this operation and is never assumed successful without remote evidence. A dryRun may plan and reconcile but cannot mutate. A revision fence mismatch, protected-branch violation, stale review, or missing approval stops the saga.
contract.budgets: Aggregate caller budget takes precedence over skill and retry budgets; attempts, remote mutations, comments, PRs, wall time, and compensation are counted globally across resumes. Exhaustion returns budget-exceeded with the last checkpoint and reconciliation evidence.
contract.boundary: Stay within the skill's declared scope, trust tier, and side-effect policy. Do not broaden scope without explicit user direction.
contract.rejection-policy: Validate every artifact against its declared JSON schema before emission. An invalid artifact is rejected and never passed downstream; record the rejection as a structured reason: {artifactType, schemaErrors[], attempt}. Retry a rejected artifact at most 3 attempts. The retry prompt keeps only the first format-error message and omits all prior format errors (SWE-agent ACI retry guardrail). Never drop a result silently: narrate an empty result explicitly ("ran successfully, no output") instead of emitting nothing.
